0.0.n: A polite way to indicate the dish being presented.

0.1.n: Part of 海ぶどう, the name of an edible seaweed with tiny beadlike clusters.

0.2.n: Together with 海, this names a seaweed, not actual fruit.

0.3.n: A polite ending identifying the dish; the topic particle は is omitted after こちら.

0.4.n: Adds a friendly, shared-confirmation tone to the introduction.

1.0.n: Names the citrus-based dipping sauce available with the dish.

1.1.n: Marks ポン酢 as the thing that is available.

1.2.n: Polite form of ある, used here to say that sauce is provided.

1.3.n: Links the sauce's availability to the serving instruction as its reason.

1.5.n: Repeated here to specify which sauce to put on the seaweed.

1.6.n: Marks ポン酢 as what you apply to the food.

1.7.n: The て-form of つける connects putting sauce on the food with eating it.

1.8.n: Uses the respectful eating verb 召し上がる in a very polite request, typical when serving customers.

3.0.n: The first part of 海ぶどう, repeated here as the dish's name.

3.1.n: Completes 海ぶどう, whose name reflects the seaweed's resemblance to tiny grapes.

0.lit: This here is sea grapes, you see.
0.tip: 海ぶどう is one food name, even though the subtitle splits it into 海 and ぶどう.

1.lit: Since there is ponzu sauce, apply ponzu sauce and please eat.
1.tip: The て-form links applying the sauce to eating; the food itself is understood rather than stated.

2.tip: はい can acknowledge instructions, not just answer a yes-or-no question.

3.tip: Repeating just a food's name is natural when noticing or confirming what it is.
